Troubleshooting tips

Image taken from Troubleshooting in R, Chapter 11.2 How to look for help

When stuck, do not despair! Chances are that someone else has run into the same issue before. Here are some practical steps to try and troubleshoot before reaching out for help:

1. Check R and your Environment

Before diving deep, make sure your setup is working as expected:

  • Is R itself up to date?
    • Run R.version.string to check.
    • Updating to the latest release can fix known bugs.
  • Is RStudio (or your IDE) up to date?
    • RStudio regularly patches bugs and adds features that affect package handling and rendering.
  • Are your packages installed?
    • Use installed.packages() or try library(packagename) to confirm.
    • If missing, install with install.packages("packagename").
  • Are your packages loaded?
    • Just installing a package isn’t enough — you need to load it from your library
      • library(packagename) at the top of your script or chunk.
  • Check for warnings when loading packages.
    • Warnings may indicate version conflicts, missing dependencies, or that an update is required.
  • Are packages up to date?
    • Run old.packages() to see what’s outdated
    • Update with update.packages(ask = FALSE) or point and click “Update” in the Packages tab
  • Check conflicts between packages.
    • If two packages have functions with the same name, R will use the one loaded last.
    • Use conflicted::conflict_scout() to identify overlaps.
  • Check your working directory.
    • Run getwd() to see where R is looking for files.
    • Use setwd() or the here package
    • If your code can’t find a file, it might just be looking in the wrong place.
  • Restart your R session.
    • Sometimes lingering objects or masked functions cause strange errors.
    • In RStudio: Session → Restart R or press Ctrl + Shift + F10.

2. Read the Function Manual

  • Use ?function_name or help(function_name) to pull up documentation.
# help for packages
?tidyverse
starting httpd help server ... done
# help for functions
?mutate
  • Check the Examples section at the bottom of help pages — often the quickest way to see correct usage.
  • Try example(function_name) to run a few built-in demos.
Note

example() only works with packages that provided examples of use**

example(summary)

summry> summary(attenu, digits = 4) #-> summary.data.frame(...), default precision

3. Look for Clues in Error Messages

  • Don’t ignore error messages — read them carefully.
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  age = c("25", "thirty", "40"))

# try to convert age to numeric
df$age_num <- as.numeric(df$age)
Warning: NAs introduced by coercion

  • Break them down: they usually tell you what object is missing, what type is expected, or where the code broke.

    • In this example, R couldn’t turn some of the values into numbers
    • Inspect the data, in this case “thirty” would need to be converted to 30

  • If the message is unclear, copy the exact text into a search engine or Stack Overflow.

df2 <- data.frame(
  site = c("A", "B", "C"),
  var1 = c(1, 2, 3),
  var2 = c(4, 5, 6))

# Try to standardize multiple columns
df2 %>% 
  mutate(across(var1, var2, as.numeric()))
Error in `mutate()`:
ℹ In argument: `across(var1, var2, as.numeric())`.
Caused by error:
! object 'var2' not found

In this example we can search something like: “mutate across columns as.numeric”

  • The AI summary has a suggested fix we can try, or we can click through the links to find a solution
df2 %>%
  mutate(across(c(var1, var2), as.numeric))
  site var1 var2
1    A    1    4
2    B    2    5
3    C    3    6

4. Simplify the Problem

  • Reproduce the issue with the smallest possible piece of code (a “minimal reproducible example”).
  • Run the code incrementally, execute line by line or in small chunks
  • This often reveals the problem right away. If not, it makes it easier for others to help you.

5. Search Before You Ask

  • Google or search Stack Overflow.
  • Include “R” + function name + error message in your search (see example above)
  • R has been around a long time — many issues already have answers online.

6. Leverage R Resources

  • RStudio Community
  • CRAN package vignettes (vignette(“packagename”))
  • Cheatsheets from Posit (R Cheatsheets)

7. Asking for Help (Last Step)

If you’ve tried the above and still need help:

  • Provide a clear description of the problem.
  • Include code or example code with the issue.
  • Mention what you’ve already tried.

Another option:

  • using AI

    • https://claude.ai/
Warning

Be mindful of AI tools, they can hallucinate and produce responses that are not useful. Do not include sensitive information in your queries. Image source

Asking for help on online forums:

https://stackoverflow.com/help/how-to-ask
